Unit 4 — Heroes

Part I — Continuous paragraph listening

Continuous paragraph listening

Listen to each complete textbook paragraph or connected list first. Then study its individual sentences below.

Page 50 · Unit opener
Heroes inspire us and help shape a better world.
In this unit, let's explore heroes from different times.
What makes a hero?
Is it the courage to protect the nation?
Or is it taking responsibility in difficult situations?
Or is it doing the hard work to improve people's lives?
By the end of this unit, you will make a short video about a local hero.
Page 50 · Learning objectives
After completing the unit, you will be able to:
use words and expressions in the unit to talk about heroes.
use attributive clauses with who to tell stories of heroes.
describe the qualities of heroes.
Page 51 · Dictionary entries
O Read the dictionary entries and answer the questions.
hero /ˈhɪərəʊ/ (heroes) noun [C] A hero is someone who has done something brave, new, or good, and who is therefore greatly admired by a lot of people.
hero /ˈhɪərəʊ/ (heroes) noun [C] If you describe someone as your hero, you mean that you admire them very much, usually because of a certain quality or skill that they have.
1 Which one do you agree with more?
2 In your opinion, what is a hero?
Page 52 · Vocabulary prompts
hero　great fighter　brave soldier　give in　with great respect　live forever　country
Page 52 · Zhao Yiman · Paragraph 1
1 As a little girl, I was often told, "Your grandmother Zhao Yiman was a hero."
However, to me, she was just a black-and-white picture on the wall.
She died long before I was born.
So, I never got to know her.
According to my great-aunt, she was a kind person who always thought of others first.
Page 52 · Zhao Yiman · Paragraph 2
2 In my teenage years, Grandma appeared in my textbooks as a great fighter.
My teacher said that she was a brave soldier who never gave in.
She didn't say a word even when she was badly hurt by the enemy.
Page 53 · Zhao Yiman · Paragraph 3
3 Years later, I followed Grandma's footsteps across China.
She fought in many places.
I saw Yiman Street, Yiman Park and Yiman Primary School, all named after her.
Even now, people speak of her with great respect.
I realised that Zhao Yiman was a hero who would live forever in Chinese people's hearts.
Page 53 · Zhao Yiman · Paragraph 4
4 After I became a mother myself, I started to wonder, "How could a woman who loved her young son leave him behind?"
In a letter from Grandma to my father, I found the answer.
Between the lines, I saw a gentle mother who chose to give her life for her country.
Page 53 · The letter · Header
2 August 1936
Ning'er,
Page 53 · The letter · Paragraph 1
It's a pity that I can't complete my duty.
As a mother, I should bring you up.
But for the victory of our country, I have to give up my life today.
I can't see you again.
I just hope that you can grow up healthy.
I'll always be happy to know that.
Page 53 · The letter · Paragraph 2
My dearest boy, I won't be able to teach you through my words.
I can only teach you through my actions.
When you grow up, never forget that I died for our country.
Page 53 · The letter · Closing
Your mother,
Zhao Yiman

Page 55 · Grammar diary
10 October 2026 Sunny
Today, I interviewed an old soldier [1] in the Battle at Lake Changjin.
As a history lover, I felt very excited.
I once read about the battle.
But it was still a real shock to hear the story from a survivor.
He said the temperature then was as low as -40°C with strong winds and heavy snow.
Life was so hard for those soldiers [2] But they stayed at their posts on the front line.
Many of them lost their lives.
The soldiers [3] had their places taken by others, again and again.
My eyes grew wet as I listened to the old man.
I was deeply moved by those soldiers [4].
They are true heroes.
10 October 2026 Sunny
Today, I interviewed an old soldier who survived in the Battle at Lake Changjin.
As a history lover, I felt very excited.
I once read about the battle.
But it was still a real shock to hear the story from a survivor.
He said the temperature then was as low as -40°C with strong winds and heavy snow.
Life was so hard for those soldiers who had little to eat for days But they stayed at their posts on the front line.
Many of them lost their lives.
The soldiers who fell had their places taken by others, again and again.
My eyes grew wet as I listened to the old man.
I was deeply moved by those soldiers who gave everything for China.
They are true heroes.

Page 57 · DID YOU KNOW?
In all societies and at all times, people respect heroes and heroic actions.
Nowadays, many awards are given to people for their heroic actions.
The Touching China award is one such award.
Page 57 · Learning to learn · Inferring
Learning to learn — Inferring: We sometimes need to guess a speaker's thoughts, feelings or opinions. We call this inferring. Does the speaker's voice show any feelings? Is the speaker certain? Noticing the way people speak can help us understand them better.

Page 58 · Phonetics in use · Linking sounds (2)
Phonetics in use — Linking sounds (2): In spoken English, when one word ends with a vowel and the next word starts with a vowel, we can link the vowel sounds together with another sound. For example, when we say in the end, it can sound like in theyend.

Page 59 · Learning to learn · Introducing quotations
Learning to learn — Introducing quotations: When we quote someone, we repeat their words to share their ideas. We can use verbs such as said, stated and noted to introduce their exact words.
Page 60 · Yuan Longping · Paragraph 1
The dreamer of plenty
1 Under the hot sun, an old man walked slowly through green rice fields.
He picked an ear of rice, looked at it carefully and moved on.
It was just a normal day at work for him.
He worked from morning to night, checking countless rice plants.
His name was Yuan Longping.
Page 60 · Yuan Longping · Paragraph 2
2 Yuan was born in Beijing in 1930.
When he was young, he felt sad to discover that many Chinese people suffered from hunger.
After he left college in 1953, he spent nearly 70 years working hard to solve this problem.
Pages 60–61 · Yuan Longping · Paragraph 3
3 Yuan believed deeply that "food is the most important thing in the world".
He dreamt of developing rice plants that produce more.
However, it was easier said than done.
Over 3,000 experiments failed.
"Failure is very common in scientific research," he once said.
"Every time I fall down, I'll get up and try again."
He travelled around China to realise his dream.
He said, "I never stopped, like a bird going after the warmth of the sun."
Finally, he succeeded in developing new types of rice plants.
One produced about 20% more rice than normal plants.
Another could grow in poor soil.
Page 61 · Yuan Longping · Paragraph 4
4 But Yuan didn't stop there.
He had an even greater dream: a rice plant that would feed the whole world.
Later, age made it more difficult for him to work.
Yuan just moved his house next to the rice fields!
Page 61 · Yuan Longping · Paragraph 5
5 Yuan passed away in 2021, but his dreams live on.
Today, his rice is grown across China and in about 70 other countries.
Yuan is remembered as a national hero who helped build China into a modern socialist country.
His example continues to encourage people to follow in his footsteps.

Page 63 · Writing Step 1
Write an introduction to the life of another hero.
Step 1　Choose a hero to write about. Then answer the questions.
Introduction to the life of a hero
1 When and where was he / she born?
2 What was his / her dream?
3 What did he / she do to realise the dream and make the world better?
4 What made him / her a hero?
5 What influence has he / she had on others and the society?
Page 63 · Writing Step 2
Step 2　Organise your ideas based on the questions. Then write your introduction.
Page 63 · Writing Step 3
Step 3　Check. Did you:
□ include the main information about the person's life and his / her achievement?
□ use the words and expressions from the reading passage?
□ give your opinion about what makes a hero?
Page 63 · Writing Step 4
Step 4　Share your introduction with the class.
Page 64 · Presenting ideas
Presenting ideas
Make a short video about a local hero.
Page 64 · Presenting ideas Step 1
Step 1　Read the following quote and discuss its meaning. Then think of a local hero for your video.
A promising nation cannot be without heroes, and a promising country cannot be without pioneers.
— President Xi Jinping
Page 64 · Presenting ideas Step 2
Step 2　Organise your ideas with the help of the following outline and prepare an introduction for your video. You may use the following language tips or find useful expressions or sentences from this unit.
Opening　Introducing the person
— I am going to introduce you to a true local hero. His / Her name is...
Body
Giving the basic information
— He / She was born in...
— He / She spent... years...
Describing the person's actions
— He / She gave everything for...
— He / She stayed calm in the face of danger.
— He / She worked from morning to night.
Explaining why the person is a hero
— He / She is a(n)... who never gave in / took responsibility in difficult situations / ...
— His / Her example continues to encourage...
— His / Her efforts have helped...
Conclusion　Giving your opinion on this person
— I was deeply moved by...
— He / She is a true hero.
Page 65 · Presenting ideas Steps 3–4
Step 3　Record your voice-over for the video. Present your video to the class.
Step 4　Vote on the best three videos.

What makes a hero?

Chinese translation

是什么造就了英雄？

No key vocabulary or phrase selected for this item.

本句没有需要特别讲解的重点词汇或短语。

Sentence structure

Wh-question: question word + auxiliary/be + subject + main verb/complement.

中文帮助：疑问句：疑问结构（What makes a hero），应结合原句定位疑问成分、主语和谓语。

Grammar point

Notice the tense, subject–verb agreement, and the function of each phrase in context.

中文帮助：注意句子的时态、主谓一致，以及各个短语在语境中的作用。

How to use this pattern

Use the same question pattern to ask for information or an opinion.

Extra example

What can we learn from this old object?

我们能从这件古老的物品中学到什么？

5

Is it the courage to protect the nation?

Chinese translation

是保卫国家的勇气吗？

courage

Pronunciation (IPA): UK: /ˈkʌrɪdʒ/　US: /ˈkɜːrɪdʒ/

protect

Pronunciation (IPA): UK: /prəˈtekt/　US: /prəˈtekt/

中文释义：保护

Sentence structure

Yes/No question: auxiliary or be comes before the subject.

中文帮助：一般疑问句：句首助动词、情态动词或 be 动词（Is），主语（it），主要动词或补语核心（the），宾语或补语（courage to protect the nation）。

Grammar point

The to-infinitive can express purpose or complete the meaning of another word.

中文帮助：动词不定式可以表示目的，或补充说明另一个词的含义。

How to use this pattern

Use the same question pattern to ask for information or an opinion.
